column1: The Necessity and Purpose of Elections

column2: Representative Democracy: Citizens govern through elected representatives in large societies

column3: Law-Makers: Voters choose who will make laws
Government Formation: Voters decide who will form the government
Policy Direction: Voters select which party’s policies will guide governance

column2: Universal Adult Franchise: One person, one vote, one value
Real Choice: Multiple political parties and candidates must be free to contest
Regular Intervals: Elections must be held periodically
People’s Preference: Candidate preferred by voters must win
Free and Fair Process: Voters must vote without fear, pressure, or manipulation

column3: Factionalism: Creates disunity and rivalry in society
Unhealthy Practices: Use of dirty tricks and false allegations

column2: Policy Impact: Long-term policies may suffer

column3: Incentive to Perform: Parties must serve people to win elections
Public Accountability: Poor performance leads to electoral defeat
Lok Sabha Constituencies: 543 constituencies elect Members of Parliament
State Assembly Constituencies: MLAs elected at the state level
Scheduled Castes: 84 Lok Sabha seats reserved
Scheduled Tribes: 47 Lok Sabha seats reserved
Local Bodies: One-third seats reserved in rural and urban local bodies
Legislatures: One-third seats reserved under Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (2023)
Electoral Roll: Includes all citizens aged 18 and above
Universal Inclusion: No discrimination based on caste, religion, or gender
Eligibility: Candidate must be a voter and at least 25 years old
Affidavit Requirement: Disclosure of criminal cases, assets, liabilities, and education

column2: Campaign Period: Two weeks between final candidate list and polling day

column3: Religious Neutrality: No use of religious places for campaigning
Government Resources: Ban on use of official vehicles and aircraft
Ministerial Restrictions: No foundation stones after election announcement
Ballot System: Earlier method using ballot papers
Electronic Voting Machines: Present system using EVMs

column1: Why Elections in India are Democratic

column3: Autonomous Body: Independent of government control
Role of CEC: Appointed by President, not answerable to government
Control of Elections: Manages elections from announcement to results
Voter Turnout: Stable or increasing participation
Social Inclusion: Higher turnout among poor and illiterate voters
Peaceful Transfers: Ruling parties often lose elections
Public Verdict: Results accepted by defeated parties

column1: Challenges to Free and Fair Elections

column2: Money Power: Wealthy candidates gain unfair advantage
Criminal Connections: Candidates with criminal backgrounds enter politics
Dynastic Politics: Political power concentrated in families
Lack of Choice: Similar policies among major parties limit real options
